items.title: Bley Carla — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Gary Burton wanted to do an album... I wrote Gary Burton’s quartet into it... we practiced it, we rehearsed it out in California... and recorded it in New York.

ctx.x: I’ve known Steve Swallow most of my life and he used to commission me to write a piece. He paid $50 for every piece I would write. Just you know to support the arts, and, Gary... I had just, I had written a song called A Genuine Tong Funeral, and I tried everywhere to get it, a record company, to agree to record it. I went to Blue Note, I went to Columbia, I went to everyone I knew. And everybody said no. So it just sat there on the shelf, and all of the sudden Gary Burton wanted to do an album, and Steve…

Can I go back to A Genuine Tong Funeral and the one thing I want to address here, makes me think that your, not just your composing life was continuing to grow and expand, but as a pianist was starting to become part of the factor there too. Because you’re listed on here in the personnel, as... and maybe you’re listed as... Well, it’s Gary Burton, Vibraphone, Carla Bley, piano, organ, and conductor.

items.doc: Gary Burton NEA Jazz Master Oral History Interview-1
items.title: Gary Burton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I’ve watched quite a few of my friends and co-performers, collaborators—Carla Bley, Chick Corea, Keith Jarrett and so on—be given this honor in recent years.

ctx.x: Ok. I saw you two or three weeks ago. You had just been honored NEA Jazz Master. What was that feeling... Tell me your reaction when you first learned you became an NEA Jazz Master.

Well, it was not a total surprise, because I’ve watched quite a few of my friends and co-performers, collaborators—Carla Bley, Chick Corea, Keith Jarrett and so on—be given this honor in recent years. So I’ve said to myself, “Well, there’s probably a chance that I might get called one of these days.” So it didn’t totally come out of the blue, but nonetheless felt great to hear that I had been chosen for my career, for my life, to be honored in this way. Other people have asked me about what it means. One thing I…
In the performance at the Kennedy Center, Chick Corea, who has been one of your long-time musical partners...
